r0.why: Unicellular ciliate, three habitats, stagnant ponds, 0.06-0.3 mm and shapes all match [1],[2],[14],[15].

r1.why: Easy culture/conjugation hence classroom use, lab rats of Ciliophora, late-17th-c. observation, Huygens 1678, slipper animalcule, Hill 1752 from Greek oblong all in cited sentences.

r2.why: Stiff elastic pellicle, three layers, hexagonal/rectangular depressions with one cilium each, trichocysts with non-toxic defensive filaments match [16]-[20].

r3.why: Rows of cilia, fast stiff effective and slow curling recovery stroke, grain-field waves, spiralling, reversing and retrying (avoidance reaction) match [28]-[34].

r4.why: More than half its energy on propulsion, under 1% efficient, near theoretical maximum for short cilia match [35]-[37]; 'expensive' follows directly.

r5.why: Bacteria/algae/yeasts, continuously beating cilia-lined oral groove, gullet, cytostome, food vacuoles in cyclosis, enzymes, pH 7 to 3 in five minutes match cited sentences.

r6.why: Osmotic inflow expelled by contractile vacuoles, number varies by species, a few species gain nutrients from endosymbiotic chlorella match [25]-[27].
